title: Wide Field Imager view of the spiral galaxy NGC 3621
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 3621, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope
celestial: NGC 3621 · constellation Hydra · about 22 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This is the spiral galaxy NGC 3621, photographed with the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope's Wide Field Imager at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile. It lies about 22 million light-years away, in Hydra, the Sea Snake.

NGC 3621 is comparatively bright for a galaxy, so it can be seen well even through moderate-sized telescopes. Like other spirals, it is a flattened disc of stars, gas and dust, arranged in arms around a brighter center.

Its data were not taken specifically for this image but already sat in the ESO archive, where Joe DePasquale picked them out for the Hidden Treasures competition. Archives like ESO's hold enormous amounts of observations, and competitions like this one encouraged people to dig through them and turn raw data into finished pictures.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (27.99 x 24.77 arcminutes) and distance (22 million light years), the frame spans roughly 179,000 × 159,000 light-years. Its light set out about 22 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was made with the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope, using several broad filters plus ones for glowing oxygen and hydrogen. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Through a moderate-sized telescope the galaxy is visible, but long exposures bring out far more detail and color than the eye could.
